taste.name: Editorial Over Interface
taste.trigger: When choosing a typographic identity for a GPU utility's marketing page
taste.decision: Chose Bodoni serif display + General Sans body pairing over a uniform geometric sans-serif
taste.reason: A wallpaper engine sells an aesthetic experience, not a workflow. The Bodoni communicates that the product cares about visual taste, which is the product's core promise.
evidence: Serif reserved for headings only, never body

taste.name: Warm-Tinted Neutrals Over Pure Darks
taste.trigger: When building a dark palette for a product that runs behind desktop icons all day
taste.decision: Tinted every neutral toward amber/brown and refused any pure gray, accepting higher maintenance cost
taste.reason: Warm tinting prevents the cold-terminal feeling of pure dark UIs. Since the product lives on the desktop permanently, the palette must feel like a living room wall, not a code editor.
evidence: Zero pure grays in entire palette

taste.name: No Cards, No Shadows — Trust the Padding
taste.trigger: When organizing six effect showcases into a scrollable page
taste.decision: Refused card containers or box shadows, relying on 128px/96px section padding and background color shifts
taste.reason: On a near-black surface, card borders create clutter, not clarity. 128px of silence between sections resets the eye without needing container edges.

taste.name: Gold Scarcity Over Gold Saturation
taste.trigger: When gold (#c9a24d) is the only chromatic color in a warm-neutral palette
taste.decision: Restricted gold to 5 text elements and 25%-opacity borders, rather than saturating headings and backgrounds
taste.reason: If gold appeared everywhere it becomes neutral. By making gold rare, each gold element carries meaning. The hero headline is off-white, not gold.
